name: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT / Nhava Sheva)
significance: Largest container-handling port in India, handling over 50% of the nation's containerized cargo.
examFacts: Commissioned in 1989 to decongest the older Mumbai Port; India's premier container gateway.
Terminal station of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) connecting Dadri (UP) to JNPT.
India's first 100% landlord major port where all berths are operated under public-private partnerships (PPP).

name: Deendayal Port (Kandla)
significance: India's largest port by cargo volume handled; constructed as a major port post-1947 to compensate for the loss of Karachi Port.
examFacts: Built in the 1950s after the Partition of India when Karachi Port went to Pakistan.
Renamed as Deendayal Port in 2017; handles the largest volume of dry cargo and crude oil in India.
India's first Special Economic Zone (EPZ - Export Processing Zone) was established here in 1965.

name: Visakhapatnam Port
significance: Deepest major port on the eastern coast of India, sheltered by the famous Dolphin's Nose promontory.
examFacts: Only natural harbour on the Coromandel / Eastern Coast of India; sheltered from Bay of Bengal cyclones by Dolphin's Nose hill.
Headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command of the Indian Navy and Hindustan Shipyard.
Primary export outlet for Bailadila iron ore destined for Japan and South Korea.

name: Chennai Port (Madras Port)
significance: Second oldest major port in India after Kolkata, established in 1881; major automobile export hub ('Detroit of India').
examFacts: Entirely artificial harbour enclosed by breakwaters on an open surf-beaten coastline.
Primary automobile and rolling stock export hub of India (Hyundai, Ford, Renault-Nissan, Royal Enfield).
Connected via the Chennai-Bengaluru-Chitradurga industrial corridor.

name: Paradip Port
significance: Major port dedicated to bulk mineral exports (iron ore, coal, aluminium) from the mineral-rich hinterland of Odisha and Jharkhand.
examFacts: First major port commissioned on the East Coast of independent India, inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1962.
Located at the confluence of the Mahanadi River and the Bay of Bengal.
Handles huge quantities of thermal coal shipped to southern Indian power plants (coastal shipping corridor).

name: Cochin Port (Kochi Port)
significance: Situated on Willingdon Island and Vallarpadam within the Vembanad Lake lagoon; historic spice trade capital.
examFacts: Vallarpadam International Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) is India's first dedicated transshipment port terminal.
Strategic location on the main East-West international maritime shipping route connecting Europe/Middle East to East Asia.
Home to Cochin Shipyard Limited, builder of India's first indigenous aircraft carrier INS Vikrant.

name: Mormugao Port
significance: Premier iron ore export terminal on the mouth of the Zuari River in Goa.
examFacts: Granted major port status in 1963 following the liberation of Goa in Operation Vijay (1961).
Located at the mouth of the Zuari River; river barges transport iron ore directly from interior mines to port berths.
One of the oldest modern ports in western India, connected by rail since the Portuguese era (1888).

name: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (Kolkata / Haldia)
significance: Only riverine major port in India, located on the Hooghly River ~200 km from the Bay of Bengal.
examFacts: India's oldest operating major port, established in 1870 by the British East India Company / Calcutta Port Trust.
Comprises two dock systems: Kolkata Dock System (riverine) and Haldia Dock Complex (deep-water downstream).
Faces severe siltation requiring continuous maintenance dredging and water discharge from the Farakka Barrage on the Ganga.

name: V.O. Chidambaranar Port (Tuticorin)
significance: Strategic southern port in the Gulf of Mannar, named after celebrated freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaram Pillai.
examFacts: Named after freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, who founded the historic Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906.
All-weather port located in the rain-shadow region of the Western Ghats, functioning uninterrupted during cyclones.
Closest Indian port to the international sea routes passing through Sri Lanka (Colombo).

name: Port Blair Port (Sri Vijaya Puram)
significance: India's 13th major port, guarding the Malacca Strait and Indian Ocean SLOCs (Sea Lines of Communication).
examFacts: Declared India's 13th Major Port in 2010; capital renamed as Sri Vijaya Puram in 2024.
Headquarters of India's first and only Tri-Services Command: the Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC).
Overlooks the Six Degree Channel and Ten Degree Channel, vital international tanker choke points.
